---
title: "Datasets"
---

maplore includes three small datasets to try the components with. All of
them are `sf` objects, ready to use as a mapgl source.

| Dataset | What | Geometry | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ar_departments` | The 529 departments of Argentina, with population in 2022 and 2035 and the projected growth (`NA` for Islas del Atlántico Sur, which has no estimates) | Polygons | IGN, INDEC |
| `earthquakes` | The 2,569 earthquakes of magnitude 4.5 or more in southern South America, 2016-2025, with magnitude and depth | Points | USGS |
| `jp_prefectures` | Five prefectures of Japan, from Hokkaido to Okinawa, with population in 2020 and 2024 and the share of people aged 65 and over | Polygons | Statistics Bureau of Japan, Natural Earth |

## Stories in the data

- **Argentina** (`ar_departments`): the City of Buenos Aires is projected to
  lose 5% of its population between 2022 and 2035, while 23 of the 24
  surrounding *partidos* grow.
- **Earthquakes** (`earthquakes`): earthquakes get deeper from west to east,
  from about 56 km on the Chilean coast to about 200 km under Santiago del
  Estero, following the Nazca plate as it sinks under South America.
- **Japan** (`jp_prefectures`): a shrinking, aging country. Of the five
  prefectures, only Tokyo grew between 2020 and 2024, and in Akita almost
  40% of people are 65 or older.

## Sources and licenses

- `ar_departments`: boundaries from the Instituto Geográfico Nacional, via
  the Georef service of datos.gob.ar (CC BY 4.0); population from INDEC,
  *Estimaciones de población por sexo, departamento y año calendario
  2022-2035*.
- `earthquakes`: U.S. Geological Survey Earthquake Catalog, public domain.
- `jp_prefectures`: population from the Statistics Bureau of Japan, *Japan
  Statistical Yearbook 2026*, tables 2-3 and 2-7, used under terms
  compatible with CC BY 4.0; boundaries from Natural Earth, public domain.

The scripts that download and prepare each dataset are in the
[`data-raw`](https://github.com/JMTocho/maplore/tree/main/data-raw) folder
of the repository. See each dataset's help page, such as
`?jp_prefectures`, for its columns.

## Maps of Argentina with your own data

`ar_departments` is an example. To map Argentina with your own figures,
the [geoAr](https://politicaargentina.github.io/geoAr/) package, on CRAN,
downloads official boundaries at several levels, such as provinces,
departments and census tracts, with the INDEC codes to join your data:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(geoAr)
library(mapgl)
library(maplore)

tucuman <- get_geo("TUCUMAN")   # departments of Tucumán, with INDEC codes
# Your data, one row per department, with the same code:
tucuman <- merge(tucuman, my_data, by = "coddepto_censo")

maplibre(bounds = tucuman) |>
  add_fill_layer(id = "tucuman", source = tucuman, fill_color = "#9ecae1") |>
  add_view_summary(layer_id = "tucuman", column = "value")
```
